film: A Building on a Winter Night
line: A thermal camera circles an old apartment block on a snowy night: a leaking window, pipes inside the walls, a cat asleep on a warm bonnet, and the same block a year after its retrofit.
line_cn: 雪夜里，一台热像仪绕着一栋老居民楼转：漏风的窗、墙里的暖气管、睡在热车盖上的猫，还有一年后改造完的同一栋楼。

camera.serves: an opening; a reveal; a return to the ordinary picture

a defect; the hottest point; a single number

transitions: Transitions: scan lines, splits, level/span changes, the shutter freeze of the detector;
No cross-dissolves between visible and thermal;
no wipes that are not a sensor action.
labels: Roles: a monospace for readings, scale ends, time stamp and measurement names (IBM Plex Mono, 22–40 px); a sans for labels (Noto Sans SC for Chinese 24–40 px, Inter for English 20–32 px). OFL, self-hosted, CJK subset to the characters used.

Labels belong to the camera or to the world: a spot meter's value sits beside its crosshair; a label hangs on a leader line to the thing; the scale and the time stamp sit at the frame edges. No title bars, no centred captions.
Bilingual labels are two lines, one language each. Numbers keep one decimal and flicker in the last digit at the meter's refresh rate; the value registered for reading time is the measured median.
Nothing below 20 px at 1080p. Each label holds ≥ max(1.5 s, characters ÷ reading speed + 1.5 s) (CJK 4.5 chars/s, Latin 15 chars/s), measured from the moment it is fully on screen.
motion: 30 fps; sensor noise is new every frame, meter readouts refresh at ~6 Hz, overlays snap in with a short ease (crosshairs collapse onto their point, numbers roll up from the ambient value and land).
Heat moves the way heat moves: plumes rise and waver, breath and turbulence flicker, cooling is slow. Bodies breathe.
A scan line travels at a steady, mechanical pace (1–3 s across the frame) with a thin white edge and a faint warm glow on the thermal side.
Never moves: the scale bar and time stamp positions; a locked comparison frame.

native_moves.name: The scan line
native_moves.does: A line crosses the frame and everything behind it turns to heat (or back).
native_moves.fits: a server room at night; a kitchen before service; a forest edge at dusk.

native_moves.name: The split that travels
native_moves.does: A fixed vertical split while the camera moves: the world slides from heat into plain sight.
native_moves.fits: pipes in a floor; wiring behind a panel; blood flow under skin after exercise.

native_moves.name: Level and span
native_moves.does: Narrowing the scale until faint structure appears (veins, joists, wet patches).
native_moves.fits: underfloor heating; moisture in a ceiling; a cooling solder joint.

native_moves.name: Isotherm alarm
native_moves.does: Everything above a threshold turns one colour.
native_moves.fits: overheating breakers; fever screening of a crowd of animals; leaking seals on a cold-store door.

native_moves.name: The hot-spot tracker jumps
native_moves.does: A max marker goes to the hottest point and leaps when something new warms up; between leaps it holds still on that point.
native_moves.fits: a phone charger on a desk; an eye opening; a bearing starting to fail.

native_moves.name: Same scale, two times
native_moves.does: Before and after side by side, locked, read, judged.
native_moves.fits: a repaired roof; a fever going down; a machine after maintenance.

native_moves.name: Ghosts
native_moves.does: Heat left behind where something was: a car that drove off, a hand on a table, a body on a bed.
native_moves.fits: a crime-free mystery; who sat where; how long ago.

score.note: sparse and cold: bowed vibraphone, glass, harp, low strings; a pulse that can become a heartbeat
